gaps.sentence: ___ her age, she still runs marathons.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun (her age); the conjunctions would need a clause.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: We took the coast road ___ the motorway to enjoy the views.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + noun' marks the rejected alternative.

gaps.sentence: I know exactly what the risks are. ___, I'm going anyway.
gaps.hint: doing it in spite of risk

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ she felt nervous, she delivered a flawless speech.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a full clause and is stronger than although.

gaps.sentence: ___ feeling nervous, she delivered a flawless presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + -ing expresses concession with a non-finite form.
